Thunderbird supports instant messaging and chat using IRC, XMPP, and Google Talk.

__TOC__

= Configuring Chat =
To use Chat, you must first create a new account (or configure an existing account) with an online instant messaging or chat provider. Thunderbird currently works with IRC, XMPP, <del>Twitter</del>, and Google Talk. 

In this example we will show IRC, Google Talk and XMPP.  Note, Twitter is no longer supported.

== Start the New Account Wizard ==

At the top of the Thunderbird window, click on the {menu File} menu, then click {menu New} and then click {menu Chat Account…}:

[[Image:ChatSelectionDialog]] 

== Enter Username ==

For IRC, you will have to enter your IRC server name, e.g. irc.mozilla<!---->.org for Mozilla's IRC server.

For XMPP, you will also have to enter your XMPP server name. 

[[Image:irc-enter-username]]

== Enter Password ==

Enter the password for the service.

[[Image:irc-password]]

{note}A password is optional for an IRC account and is only required if you have reserved your nickname on the IRC network.{/note}

== Advanced Options ==
This is not usually needed, so just click {for win,linux}{button Next}{/for}{for mac}{button Continue}{/for}.

[[Image:irc-skip-advanced-options]]

== Finish the Wizard ==

Next, you will be presented with a Summary screen. Click {button Finish} to finish the wizard and start chatting.

[[Image:irc-summary]]

= Using Chat =

== Connect to your Chat Account ==
First make sure that you are online by going to your Chat Status and connecting:
* click on the {menu Tools} menu and then click on {menu Chat status} and then {menu Show Accounts…}
* click on the {button Connect} button next to the account you want to go online with

[[Image:irc-click-connect]]

== Use the Chat Tab to start and join conversations ==
Click on the Chat Tab next to the Write Tab to start and join conversations.

[[Image:irc-chat-tab]]

== Chat is included in Search ==

Like any other type of Thunderbird account (e.g. email and RSS), Chat is integrated with search.

Here's an example of email, and Chat conversations being found by Thunderbird's [[Global Search|global search]]:
